file_name: Nystrom DT - 2018 - Methods for Patient Centered Interface Design of Test Result Display in Online Portals.txt

barriers.description: The usability evaluation had a low sample size and a participant pool heavily skewed toward people with prior healthcare work experience, limiting the representativeness of user input.
barriers.justification: These participant-sampling constraints directly hindered designers' ability to manage and deepen user understanding, facilitate broad user involvement, and robustly evaluate designs across diverse user groups.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Aside from a low sample size, the main limitation of the user testing portion of our evaluation is the lack of a homologous “stimuli” to test with participants. An additional limitation that may affect the generalizability of the results of this study is the large percentage (71 percent) of patients who had history of working in health care prior to participating in this study.

barriers.description: The team used a semi-structured design process without a strict schedule for testing and making improvements, which increased production speed but reduced experimental rigor.
barriers.justification: This methodological choice constrained the designers' ability to conduct rigorous, controlled evaluations and to systematically integrate feedback and iteration, reducing the reliability of design evaluation activities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: In the current study, we chose to implement a semi-structured design process that refrained from using a strict schedule to determine when to begin testing and making interface improvements during the design of the interface. This methodology increased the speed at which the interface could be produced at the cost of rigorous experimental design.

barriers.description: After equalizing visual ranges for different biomarkers, the designers created non-linear scales but did not assess how those non-linear representations affected patient perceptions.
barriers.justification: Failing to evaluate the impact of non-linear scales prevented designers from fully evaluating the holistic user experience and understanding potential unintended consequences of visual design changes.
barriers.reference_excerpt: An unanticipated consequence of this design adjustment was the creation of non-linear scales, where the visual space for each biomarker are radically different than the other. We did not make any attempt to assess the impact of these non-linear scales on patient perceptions.
